description: Selected scoped claim/argument/evidence links, not exhaustive assurance or certification. Check references identify configured obligations; only a passing complete results.json with current input hashes establishes execution evidence. Assumptions and limits remain part of every claim.

claims.claim: Imported save-admission transitions conserve admitted request reservations and their abstract weighted cost, and partition logical offers into admitted/rejected outcomes.
claims.argument: Ghost counters update independently at actual Submit/Cancel/Expire/Resolve actions; compare them with the imported authoritative held set and cost function. Check imported Next correspondence and mutation-sensitive omissions, duplicate refunds, premature refunds and wrong units.
claims.conditions: Four one-shot requests, two resource classes, fixed modeled costs, five-transition horizon; safe-disposition evidence is supplied by the imported Resolve contract.
claims.limit: No repeated operation IDs, actual telemetry accuracy, physical memory, arbitrary-length histories, provider-truth or service theorem.

claims.claim: A fixed recipient diagnostic projection masks modeled hidden existence and private identity differences and rechecks current release context after preparation.
claims.argument: Compose actual Disclosure steps with one prepare/drain pair, compare both recipient output sequences, and freeze delivery-time permission/epoch/disposal/hidden-divergence facts. Witnesses require those facts, not later core changes, and masking requires authorized Health delivery. Regression paths reach legacy false-positive states while the strengthened witnesses remain false. Diagnostics stutter the core; deliberately exposed private tags/counts and epoch bypass must fail.
claims.conditions: Same public action schedule, four imported core steps, one diagnostic delivery; private identity/existence are excluded from this profile's permitted operational disclosures.
claims.limit: No timing/resource/cache side-channel guarantee, anonymity or universal unlinkability; no retroactive revocation, physical erasure, legal compliance or complete LINDDUN analysis. Imported revocation changes epoch too, so isolated grant-check sensitivity is not established here.

claims.claim: Every job in a closed finite cooperative backlog eventually receives a disposition under weak fairness of service.
claims.argument: Service removes exactly one pending job, the natural pending cardinality decreases, and non-service actions cannot increase it. Weak fairness prevents perpetual stuttering while service is enabled. Removing fairness must admit an unfinished infinite behavior.
claims.conditions: Two/three initial jobs, no arrivals/retries/new descendants, finite cancellation/invalidation state, cooperative service and explicit WF_vars(Serve). No transition-horizon cutoff is used.
claims.limit: Not a refinement of the engine or host scheduler, open-workload fairness, numeric latency/service bounds, guaranteed applied success or native preemption.

claims.claim: Pending and terminal dispositions partition the modeled backlog; applied outcomes require current uncancelled work and cancellation intent alone does not discharge it.
claims.argument: Check the identity-level partition, stable terminal outcomes and captured acceptance-time facts. Silent dropping, stale success and cancellation-as-discharge each violate a named invariant. Applied, superseded and cancelled are separate legitimate outcomes, not interchangeable successes/errors.
claims.conditions: The fixed cooperative service model classifies each job at its service boundary; dependency correctness is represented by a boolean current fact.
claims.limit: No semantic dependency oracle, public RED/SLI schema, numeric objective, physical-resource ledger or production implementation proof.
